did: I researched how home keeps its database safe, from the server's code: one SQLite file, a checked copy before every migration with the newest five kept on the same disk, a rollback that never touches the data, and no copy off the machine. I first wrote a narrated cards essay. When you turned it into a conversation, I wrote Kokoro's answers to your eight questions as an assessment rather than a to-do list, covering what a dead disk or a box that won't boot would lose, and ending with how far it would ever need to go, framed as a proposal, not a fact. Main refused the essay, so I added a questions spoken card, which sits anywhere in an essay inside the chapter before it. An independent review found seven things to fix, I fixed them, and the change merged as #3328. The essay validates and is published in testing as home-database-safety-2026-11-21.

calls.title: How a question-and-answer card fits a cards essay
options: A questions category that sits anywhere and opens no chapter of its own
An optional chapter title on every spoken card
The whole essay as one introduction card at the front
calls.why: Each chapter keeps one chapter line and one mark, and an introduction still opens its essay; one front card can hold only six exchanges, and must come first.
calls.undo: Remove questions from SPOKEN_CATEGORIES and SPOKEN_CATEGORY_OPENS in video-render (C831).

left: Studio's paste can't yet mark a questions card where you ask and Kokoro answers, because a QUESTION line means what Kokoro asks; this essay names its takes in its cut list instead, so it didn't need it.
Why SQLite was chosen isn't written down anywhere I found, and the essay says so.
